Consider the diagram below with four shapes:
A RED shape at the bottom-left.
A GREEN shape at the top-left.
A BLUE shape at the top-right.
A PURPLE shape at the bottom-right

var pointStyle = { fixed:true, visible:false }; var recType = {#redShape#}; var paraType = {#greenShape#}; var triType = {#blueShape#}; var quadType = {#purpShape#}; var PA = board.create("point", [0,0], pointStyle); var PB = board.create("point", [-2,0], pointStyle); if (recType == "square") { var PC = board.create("point", [-2,-2], pointStyle); var PD = board.create("point", [0,-2], pointStyle); } else if (recType == "rectangle") { var PC = board.create("point", [-2,-3], pointStyle); var PD = board.create("point", [0,-3], pointStyle); }; if (paraType == "rhombus") { var PE = board.create("point", [-0.75,Math.sqrt(2.4375)], pointStyle); var PF = board.create("point", [1.25,Math.sqrt(2.4375)], pointStyle); } else if (paraType == "parallelogram") { var PE = board.create("point", [0,4], pointStyle); var PF = board.create("point", [2,4], pointStyle); }; if (triType == "equilateral") { var circleA = board.create("circle", [PA, PF], {visible:false}); var circleF = board.create("circle", [PF, PA], {visible:false}); var PG = board.create("intersection", [circleA,circleF], pointStyle); } else if (triType == "isosceles") { var pointAF = [PA.X()*1/5 + PF.X()*4/5, PA.Y()*1/5 + PF.Y()*4/5]; var circleA = board.create("circle", [PA, pointAF], {visible:false}); var circleF = board.create("circle", [PF, PA], {visible:false}); var PG = board.create("intersection", [circleA,circleF], pointStyle); } else if (triType == "right-angled") { var midAF = [PA.X()*1/2 + PF.X()*1/2, PA.Y()*1/2 + PF.Y()*1/2]; var circleAF = board.create("circle", [midAF, PA], {visible:false}); var pointAF = [PA.X()*1/5 + PF.X()*4/5, PA.Y()*1/5 + PF.Y()*4/5]; var circleA = board.create("circle", [PA, pointAF], {visible:false}); var PG = board.create("intersection", [circleA, circleAF], pointStyle); board.create("angle", [PF, PG, PA], { fixed:true, highlight:false, radius:0.25, withLabel:false }); }; if (quadType == "kite") { var circleG = board.create("circle", [PG, PA], {visible:false}); var circleD = board.create("circle", [PD, PA], {visible:false}); var PH = board.create("intersection" , [circleD, circleG], pointStyle) } else if (quadType == "trapezium") { if (recType == "square") { var PH = board.create("point", [PG.X(),-3], pointStyle); } else if (recType == "rectangle") { var PH = board.create("point", [PG.X(),-2], pointStyle); }; }; var shapeWidth = Math.max(PG.X(), PH.X()) + 4; var shapeHeight = PE.Y() - Math.min(PD.Y(), PH.Y()) + 2; if (shapeWidth >= shapeHeight) { board.setBoundingBox([ -3, (PE.Y() + Math.min(PD.Y(), PH.Y()) + shapeWidth)/2, shapeWidth - 3, (PE.Y() + Math.min(PD.Y(), PH.Y()) - shapeWidth)/2 ]); } else if (shapeWidth < shapeHeight) { board.setBoundingBox([ (Math.max(PG.X(), PH.X()) - 2 - shapeHeight)/2, PE.Y() + 1, (Math.max(PG.X(), PH.X()) - 2 + shapeHeight)/2, Math.min(PD.Y(), PH.Y()) - 1 ]); polyStyle.fillColor = "green"; polyStyle.borders.strokeColor = "green"; board.create("polygon", [PA, PB, PE, PF], polyStyle); polyStyle.fillColor = "purple"; polyStyle.borders.strokeColor = "purple"; board.create("polygon", [PA, PG, PH, PD], polyStyle); polyStyle.fillColor = "blue"; polyStyle.borders.strokeColor = "blue"; board.create("polygon", [PA, PF, PG], polyStyle); var angleStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, radius:0.5, name:"\\(\\alpha\\)", withLabel:true, label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black", fontSize:15, offset:[10,0], useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; truefeedback.text:
Here is a worked solution:

Since the green shape is a {@greenShape@}, the opposite angles are equal and the sum of all the angles is \(360^\circ\).
Therefore, the green angle at the centre of the diagram is \(\frac{360 - 2\alpha}{2} = 180 - \alpha\)

Since the blue triangle is {@blueShape@}, {@if blueShape="equilateral" then "all the the angles are equal to \\(60^\\circ\\)" else if blueShape="isosceles" then "the two base angles are equal and the sum of all the angles is \\(180^\\circ\\)" else "there is a \\(90^\\circ\\) angle and the sum of all the angles is \\(180^\\circ\\)"@}.
Therefore the blue angle at the centre of the diagram is \({@if blueShape="equilateral" then "60" else if blueShape="isosceles" then sconcat("\\frac{180-",string(triAngle),"}{2} =",string(90-triAngle/2)) else sconcat("180-90-",string(triAngle)," = ",string(90-triAngle))@}^\circ\).

The four angles at the centre of the diagram form a circle, so they must sum to \(360^\circ\).
Therefore, \(90 + (180 - \alpha) + {@if blueShape="equilateral" then "60" else if blueShape="isosceles" then 90-triAngle/2 else 90-triAngle@} + \beta = 360\)

Rearranging this gives: \(\beta - \alpha = {@tans5@}\).
